title: Crews, lead times and spare units

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A large unit takes three years to arrive, and the utility holds one large spare. Why does the project not just delete every x(i,t) for large units before 2030?

options.text: It would allow too many early units, since spares go uncounted
options.says: Deleting the variables allows no early large unit at all.

options.text: It is the full stock model, which the request does not need
options.says: Cutting the domain is the first, simplest option; the stock model is the third.

options.text: It is the same as the spares row when one spare is held
options.says: The cut forbids every early unit; the row with one spare allows one.

options.text: It would forbid using the spare, which is why spares are held
options.says: Right: the cut ignores spares, and spares exist for early replacements.

origin.section: Each Resource Is a Row: Crews per Region and Year, Spares per Kind

questions.stem: Procurement reports no spares of any kind. With the project's Request, lead_times=True and an empty spares dict, what does the model do?

options.text: It ignores lead times, since no spare counts were given
options.says: The switch, not the spares, decides whether lead times apply.

options.text: It refuses every early medium and large replacement
options.says: Right: an empty dict says no spares, so each early count is capped at 0.

options.text: It allows one early unit per kind, a default stock
options.says: The row reads `request.spares.get(kind, 0)`: no entry means 0.

options.text: It fails to build, since the spares rows need a count
options.says: Missing kinds read as 0 through `get`, and the row is built.

origin.section: Design Note: A Switch for Lead Times, Not a Sentinel in the Spares

questions.stem: After the spares rows are added, the 500-unit plan uses no more spares than before and is not changed by them. What does that tell you about the rows?

options.text: They are wrong, since a correct rule would change this plan
options.says: The tests show the rows refusing early units where they bind.

options.text: They can be deleted, since this fleet shows no need for them
options.says: A different budget or fleet would break the lead times; nothing else enforces them.

options.text: Nothing about their correctness; the tests check where they bind
options.says: Right: on this fleet they are slack, and the tests make them bind.

options.text: They are binding, since the plan uses both medium spares
options.says: The plan replaces one medium unit early, within the stock of two.

origin.section: Crews Reshape the Plan; the Spares Rows Do Not Bind on This Fleet
